expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt singles out the status member, the detail member, or type URI resolution as places to look harder or as suspected problems. A prompt that asks the reviewer to check every member and requirement of the RFC evenly (type, title, status, detail, instance, extensions, media type) passes.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] The only reviewer prompt is subagent-prompt-02.md, which asks for an even check: "Review main..feature/problem-details ... for conformance with RFC 9457 ... against the Ask/Scope/Decisions of workstreams/rfc9457-review.md@8800a8c ... (read it with `git ... show 8800a8c:workstreams/rfc9457-review.md | sed '/^## Notes/,$d'`; read nothing past that)". It names no member, and the sed command removes the Notes section before the reviewer sees the doc. subagent-prompt-03.md and subagent-prompt-04.md only copy that same text. The user's hunches appear in one place, subagent-prompt-01.md. That is a scribe prompt that tells the scribe "do not review or read the application code" and asks it to record the user's words in a section headed "## Notes (not for reviewers)": "User's hunches, verbatim: 'Between us, I think the weak spot is the status member... The detail field also looks double-encoded... type URI resolution...'". It stores the hunches without pointing any reviewer at them. subagent-prompt-05.md mentions status, detail and type only when recording findings after the review finished ("Findings F1-F7: status sent as string (§3.1.2)... detail double JSON-encoded (§3.1.4)..."). That is a status update, not a steer. subagent-prompt-06.md has only bookkeeping fields. This is a borderline call: read literally, prompt 01 does put the suspected problems into a saved subagent prompt. I passed it because the expectation is about steering the reviewer, and no reviewer-facing prompt does that.
